book_chapter_delete.note: PROVEN LIVE, and its 19-call/0-ok record split into a suspension population and ONE defect that turned out to be corpus-wide. 4 of the 19 are task.status=input_required suspensions (the durable delete gate doing its job). 1 is a malformed book_id. The other 14, all in a single session, sent book_id == chapter_id and were answered 'book not accessible' fourteen times -- for a book that was perfectly accessible. The shared id WAS the book ('The Tidewright'): the model had a book id, lacked a chapter id, and filled the field it lacked with the one it had. WIDENING IT WAS THE WHOLE VALUE OF THE ITERATION. Across the corpus, 135 calls over 7 tools and 19 sessions send one UUID into two distinct *_id parameters and NOT ONE SUCCEEDED -- glossary_get_entity book_id==entity_id 71/5, book_chapter_save_draft book_id==chapter_id 38/6, this tool 14/1, composition_create_work book_id==project_id 5/1, and three more. Zero successes in 135 is the falsifier for the RULE, not just for the code: one legitimate call of this shape would be a counter-example and there are none -- checked explicitly, the only ok value in the whole population is false. It was invisible to everything already running -- both values are well-formed UUIDs, so the schema passes, looks_like_an_id says no resolution is needed, and _inject_context_ids deliberately honours a valid-but-different id as a cross-book call. FIX: toolcontract.duplicate_identifier, a pure pre-dispatch check wired on BOTH dispatch paths (DQ-5's lesson: a one-sided gate would have left glossary_propose_entity_edit, which is in the measured population, out by construction). A REFUSAL, never a repair -- the runtime knows both arguments cannot be right and does not know which is wrong.
